question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum staff/child ratio for a group of infants, toddlers and 2-year-olds (birth to 36 months)? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Infants, toddlers, and 2-year-olds ... Birth to 36 months ... 1:4
notes: Ratio 1:4 with a maximum group size of 8. Groups made up only of 2-year-olds (24 to 36 months) may use 1:8 with a group of 16. Junior Aides (16-17) do not count toward infant/toddler ratios (5 CSR 25-500.102(1)(C)1.C).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum staff/child ratio for a group made up only of 3-year-olds? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 3 through 4-yearolds ... Groups composed solely of children 3 to 4 years old ... 1:10
notes: The chart row covers groups composed solely of children 3 to 4 years old (1:10, max group 20). Mixed groups that include 2-year-olds use the Type 1 (1:10, no more than four 2-year-olds) or Type 2 (1:8) rows.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum staff/child ratio for a group made up only of 4-year-olds? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 3 through 4-yearolds ... Groups composed solely of children 3 to 4 years old ... 1:10
notes: Same chart row as 3-year-olds (groups composed solely of children 3 to 4 years old): 1:10, max group 20. Children 5 and older are 1:16.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum staff/child ratio for a group made up only of children 5 years old or older (school-age)? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 5-year-olds and up ... Groups composed solely of children 5 years or older ... 1:16
notes: The chart's oldest band is 'groups composed solely of children 5 years or older' (1:16, max group 32); there is no separate band for older school-age children. In programs licensed exclusively for school-age children, multiple groups may share the same space (5 CSR 25-500.112(1)(F)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the maximum group size for a group made up only of 4-year-olds?
quote: 3 through 4-yearolds ... Groups composed solely of children 3 to 4 years old ... 1:10 ... 20
notes: Group size need not be maintained for groups of children 2 and older during outdoor play, gross motor activities in a gym or multipurpose room, meals, field trips and special events (5 CSR 25-500.112(1)(D)), or during transport (1)(E).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum age at which a caregiver counts toward the required staff/child ratios as a regular adult caregiver (not as a Junior Aide)?
quote: Caregivers eighteen (18) years of age or older shall be counted in meeting the required staff/child ratios
notes: A Junior Aide (age 16 or 17, 5 CSR 25-500.010(2)) may also count in ratio, but only under direct supervision of an adult caregiver in the same group, never as sole caregiver, and not toward infant/toddler ratios.

question: Under Missouri's licensing rules, what college education must a newly hired director of a licensed child care center with a licensed capacity of 21 to 60 children have if qualifying through education alone (without substituting work experience)?
answer: 60 college semester hours, including 12 hours in child-related courses
quote: 21—60 Children ... Sixty (60) college semester hours. Twelve (12) of the hours must be in child-related courses
notes: Alternative for this size: 24 months experience plus 12 college semester hours in child-related courses. Requirements scale with licensed capacity: up to 20 children 30 hours (6 child-related); 61-99 children 90 hours (18 child-related); 100+ children 120 hours (24 child-related). A CDA or YDC counts as 12 months experience plus 6 child-related semester hours.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, how many clock hours of child-care related training must the director and each caregiver counted in ratio complete each calendar year?
quote: shall obtain at least twelve (12) clock hours of child-care related training during each calendar year
notes: Caregivers hired after the first of the year need 1 clock hour per month of employment (3)(C). Excess hours do not carry over (3)(J). Separate safe sleep training is required every 3 years for staff of centers licensed for infants under 1 (4)(A).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum usable indoor floor space required for each preschool or school-age child?
quote: At least thirty-five (35) square feet of usable floor space shall be provided for each preschool and school-age child coming into the facility for day care
notes: Infant/toddler space: 35 sq ft per child in centers licensed for at most 20 children (no more than 4 infants/toddlers); 45 sq ft per infant/toddler in larger centers initially licensed for infant/toddler care (or adding infant/toddler space) after the rules took effect (2)(B)2.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum outdoor play area required per child using the play area at one time?
quote: A minimum of seventy-five (75) square feet of outdoor play area per child at the time of use shall be provided
notes: Per child at the time of use. The area must also hold one-third of licensed capacity at one time and be no less than 750 square feet in total.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what must the provider have from the parent before giving any medication to a child?
answer: Dated, written permission from the parent stating how long the medication may be given
quote: All medication shall be given to a child only with the dated, written permission of the parent(s) stating the length of time medication may be given
notes: Providers are not required to give medication (3)(A). Prescription medication must be in the original labeled container; nonprescription medication must be in the original container labeled by the parent.

question: How often must staff in a licensed child care center in Missouri conduct fire drills?
quote: Child care staff shall conduct at least one (1) fire drill each month
notes: Disaster drills, including tornado drills, are required at least every three months. A written record of the date, type of drill, evacuation time and number of children present must be kept.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, for at least how long must daily child attendance records be kept on file?
quote: Daily child attendance records shall be maintained and kept on file a minimum of one (1) year
notes: Individual children's records must be kept at least 1 year after the child stops attending (4); daily staff and volunteer attendance records at least 1 year (6).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, in what position must a child under 12 months of age be placed to sleep?
quote: A child under twelve (12) months of age shall be placed on his/her back to sleep
notes: Another position requires a written statement from the infant's licensed health care provider (5 CSR 25-500.132(2)(A)3). Infants who can roll both ways are placed on their backs initially but may then adopt their own position.

question: When a child is injured or has an accident at a licensed child care center in Missouri, how soon must the provider notify the child's parents?
quote: In case of accident or injury to a child, the provider shall notify the parent(s) immediately
notes: This is a deadline for notifying parents. The rulebook sets no deadline for reporting a child's injury to the licensing agency; the accident must also be noted in the child's record (5)(B). Fires must be reported immediately to the State Fire Marshal (5 CSR 25-500.087(2)(L)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, when must information on a child's immunizations (completed, in progress, or exempt) be on file?
answer: Before the child is accepted for care (at enrollment)
quote: Completion by the parent(s) of the following written information which shall be on file before the child is accepted for care: ... 5. Information indicating that the child has completed age-appropriate immunizations, is in the process of completing immunizations, or is exempt from immunization requirements
notes: Facilities caring for 10 or more children may not enroll a child who is not adequately immunized unless the child has begun the immunization process or has a medical or parent exemption on file (5 CSR 25-500.192(4)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, the licensee must have enough staff with current age-appropriate first aid and CPR certification so that there is one certified caregiver at the facility for every how many children in the licensed capacity?
quote: current certification in age-appropriate first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training for a sufficient number of child care staff to ensure that there is one (1) caregiver at the facility for every twenty (20) children in the licensed capacity
notes: In addition, at least one caregiver with current first aid and CPR certification must be on site at all times when children are present. Ratio is based on licensed capacity, not attendance.

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, how wide an aisle must be left along one long side of each child's napping cot, bed or other sleeping equipment?
quote: Sleeping equipment shall be arranged to provide at least a two foot (2’) aisle on one (1) long side of the equipment
notes: The rule sets an aisle on one long side of sleeping equipment rather than a distance between cribs/cots on all sides.

question: Under Missouri's licensing rules for child care centers, how often must the provider submit the renewal paperwork (declaration of intent to continue operating) to the department, and by when?
answer: Annually, at least 30 calendar days before the anniversary date printed on the license
quote: The provider shall submit the following to the department on an annual basis, at least thirty (30) calendar days prior to the anniversary date as printed on the license
notes: The rulebook states no fixed license term; the license stays in effect until revoked, the facility closes, ownership changes, or (for licenses not held by legal entities) the licensee dies (5 CSR 25-500.042(17)), and is renewed through the annual submission (5 CSR 25-500.052, 'procedures for license renewal').

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum age of a Junior Aide who may be counted in staff/child ratios under direct supervision of an adult caregiver?
quote: A Junior Aide is an individual sixteen (16) or seventeen (17) years of age
notes: A Junior Aide counts in ratio only under direct supervision of an adult caregiver in the same group, may not be the sole caregiver of a group or on the premises, and does not count toward infant/toddler ratios (5 CSR 25-500.102(1)(C)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, what is the minimum staff/child ratio for a mixed-age group that has no more than four children aged 24 to 36 months and at least one child older than 36 months? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Mixed ages (Type 1) 2-year-olds and older, with a maximum of four (4) 2-year-olds ... 1:10
notes: Max group size 20. With more than four 2-year-olds (Type 2) the ratio tightens to 1:8.

question: Above what daily attendance may the director of a licensed child care center in Missouri no longer be counted in staff/child ratios (except during naptime or as an emergency substitute)?
quote: If a center has an attendance of more than fifty (50) children, the center director or individual in charge shall not be included in staff/child ratios except during naptime or on an emergency substitute basis
notes: Applies when attendance is more than 50 children. Separately, if more than 30 children attend at lunch or dinner, meal preparation/serving staff are not counted in ratio during that time (3).

question: In a licensed child care center in Missouri, during naptime must the staff/child ratio be maintained inside the napping area for a group of 3-year-olds?
quote: During naptime, groups composed of children two (2) years old and older shall not be required to maintain staff/ child ratio within the napping area, but shall not exceed group size limitations
notes: Group size limits still apply in the napping area, and the required ratio must still be maintained on the premises during naptime. Does not apply to groups with children under 2.

question: During outdoor play at a licensed child care center in Missouri, may staff/child ratios be relaxed beyond the indoor ratios if a 2-year-old is present in the outdoor play space?
quote: During outdoor play, staff/child ratios may be one and one-half (1 1/2) times the indoor staff/child ratios if children two (2) years of age or younger are not present in the outdoor play space
notes: The 1.5x outdoor ratio is allowed only when no children 2 or younger are in the outdoor play space; indoor ratios must still be maintained on the premises. 5 CSR 25-500.082(6)(A)3 states the same relaxation for children 3 and above.
